reason: The immediate goal is to put the station on reserve, and the charged battery at the shutdown controls looks like the direct way to do that.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to emergency power, though this may be only one part of the shutdown.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so shutting it down also seems relevant, but I want to establish reserve power first.
The heat store should help protect the garden, but the stated first goal is the station reserve.

effect: The reserve now powers essential loads, while the fuel plant and normal garden circulation are off. The garden needs its survival equipment in the nook.
reaction: The dimming lights make the shutdown feel consequential, and I’m curious how the beds will be kept going.
reason: The outdoor water line will lose heat, so using the shutdown controls on it seems like the next practical precaution.
expectation: I expect the outdoor line to be isolated or otherwise made safe for the loss of heat, though I’m unsure exactly how.

alternatives.reason: Moving the heat store into the nook should help protect the garden, but I want to address the exposed line first.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, with its pump and thaw checks on essential power. The next goal is to move both troughs into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line before it loses heat makes practical sense; I’m curious how the garden will manage without normal circulation.
reason: The warm heat store should help prepare the nook for the two troughs.
expectation: I expect the heat store to move into the nook and release warmth there, though the troughs will still need to be moved separately.

alternatives.reason: Moving the lettuce directly would advance the new goal, but I want the heat store in place first.

effect: The heat store is now in the growing nook, preparing it for the troughs.
reaction: The result is straightforward, though it gives no detail about how much warmth the store provides.
reason: The goal calls for moving both troughs, so I’ll move the lettuce first.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed in the buffered nook; the potato trough will still need to be moved.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs to go into the nook, and either order seems reasonable.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and its common-return couplings are capped. The potato trough still needs to be moved.
reaction: Carrying the bed level and protecting its leaves makes the move feel concrete.
reason: Moving the potato trough completes the stated goal, and it is the only numbered action available.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be sheltered in the nook alongside the lettuce, with its reservoir kept underneath.

effect: Both troughs are now sheltered in the warm nook, completing the chapter’s goals. The potato bed retains its reservoir, dark cover and support.
reaction: Making room for the potato leaves gives the move a satisfying physical detail, though I’m still curious how the garden will be sustained during the storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining and isolating the outdoor water line was the most worthwhile action: it connected the loss of heat to a concrete precaution while keeping thaw checks powered.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the heat store felt less informative because the result gave no detail about how it buffered the nook.

surprise.text: Switching to reserve also stopped the garden’s normal circulation, making its protection more involved than simply keeping the cabin powered.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary. Moving the heat store before the troughs seemed sensible, although its immediate result did not explain its contribution.

continue.text: Yes. I’d want to see how the station and garden fare through the storm and what happens to the specimens bound for Earth.
